title: Hedged region tiering and GPU-class spend limiter
creator: Aisha Mendes
description: Design and implement a hedged routing controller that enforces per-tenant budget caps while selecting region tiers and preferred GPU classes. The controller should probabilistically route traffic between spot and on-demand pools based on tenant budget headroom, preemption risk score, and latency SLOs; and it must fall back to cheaper model variants (quantized or smaller architectures) when soft spend limits are reached. Key requirements: 1) per-tenant daily and rolling-1h spend caps enforceable without adding blocking latency; 2) a GPU-class scoring function that accounts for model shape, sequence length distribution, and kernel cost to pick heterogenous instance types; 3) region tiering so requests prefer nearest low-latency tier but can spill to lower-cost tier when budget constrained; 4) graceful degradation: automated, reversible fallback to model variants with observable quality regressions tracked against a held-out eval promptset; 5) telemetry and alerting: token-level cost, per-tenant spend burn rate, eviction probability heatmap, and failed-fallback counts. Deliverables: design doc, simulation harness, integration into routing service, canary rollout, dashboard panels, and runbook for incidents.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha: Scoping spike completed. Initial sim shows savings of ~23% on synthetic steady-state traffic when hedging spot/on-demand with a 10% chance of spot fallback. Need to validate with real tenant traces.

2026-02-24 - PM review (Jonas Reed): Requested explicit customer opt-in flags and a 'no-spot' tenant label for regulated customers. Also asked for a rollout knob to disable variant fallback during critical SLA windows.
2026-03-02 - Design review (Maya Chen): UX for tenant console shows spend cap slider and a fallback-variance preview. Design suggests adding a small latency penalty estimate when enabling hedge mode.

2026-03-08 - Eng sync: Decided on hybrid strategy: deterministic routing for high-priority tenants (respecting 'no-spot') and probabilistic hedging for best-effort tenants. Chosen hedging scheme: weighted coin flip based on headroom ratio (headroom / (headroom + k)).

2026-03-12 - Luca: Performance benchmarks in staging: end-to-end decision latency of router < 1.8ms p95; steady-state cost reduction ~18% vs on-demand-only with comparable p95 tail for common workloads. Opening PR for review.
